title: EMGS Visa Approval Letter (VAL) Process & Cost of Living in Kuala Lumpur for Students

runs.t: Indian students who receive an offer from a Malaysian university must complete the required immigration process before travelling to begin their studies. For many international higher-education applicants, the process is handled through Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) and the Malaysian Immigration Department. The key pre-arrival approval document is commonly called the electronic Visa Approval Letter (eVAL).

The eVAL is not the same as the final Student Pass endorsement. Students may also need a Single Entry Visa (SEV) before travel, depending on the entry requirements applicable to their nationality. After arrival, they must complete the required medical screening and follow their institution’s instructions for Student Pass endorsement.

After accepting an offer, prepare the required documents and submit the Student Pass application through EMGS or the institution’s approved process. EMGS performs document and eligibility checks and coordinates the application for Immigration consideration. Once the eVAL is issued, check whether an SEV is required for your passport, travel only in line with the approved instructions, complete the post-arrival medical screening within the specified period, and submit your passport or documents for Student Pass endorsement as directed by the university.

sections.title: What are EMGS, eVAL and the Student Pass?

rows.t: EMGS
Education Malaysia Global Services, which facilitates and manages international student application processes and related services.
It is not the university admissions office and does not itself guarantee the final Immigration decision.
eVAL
Electronic Visa Approval Letter issued following the relevant approval process. Older materials may refer to VAL.
It is not the same as the final Student Pass endorsement or a travel document in every case.
SEV
Single Entry Visa, where required for the student’s nationality and circumstances before travelling.
Not every passport holder has identical pre-arrival visa requirements. Check official instructions.
Student Pass
Immigration permission for an international student to reside in Malaysia for study at an approved institution.
It does not grant unrestricted employment rights or permission to study at any institution/course.

sections.title: Step-by-step EMGS and Student Pass process

runs.t: Receive and accept the university offer. Confirm the programme, campus, intake, fee payment deadline and the institution’s visa application process.
Prepare the documents. Ensure passport details, photograph, academic records and health declaration are accurate and consistent with the offer.
Submit the application. Follow the university’s instructions for submission through EMGS, EMGS HUB or the institution’s Student Application Registration System (STARS), as applicable.
Complete document checks and respond promptly to requests. Missing or inconsistent information can delay the process.
Wait for Immigration approval and the eVAL. Do not book non-refundable travel on the assumption that approval is certain.
Check whether you need an SEV before departure. Use the official Malaysian visa channel and the current nationality-specific rules.
Travel with the required documents. Carry the offer letter, eVAL, passport, visa where required, accommodation details and university arrival instructions.
Complete the post-arrival medical screening within the required timeframe. Follow the institution’s instructions on the appointed clinic and appointment process.
Complete Student Pass endorsement. Submit your passport or required information through the institution’s process and check that the pass details are correct.

The Education Malaysia FAQ states that the general client charter is 14 working days for a complete application, but actual processing can vary and incomplete or incorrect submissions may take longer. The Malaysian government’s digital service page separately displays a 24-working-day service duration. Treat these as service guidance, not a guaranteed end-to-end timeline: add time for university processing, document corrections, SEV issuance, travel and post-arrival formalities.

rows.t: Passport

Check validity against current Immigration requirements; Immigration’s published Student Pass page states at least 18 months for the listed higher-education category. Confirm with the university before applying.
Passport photograph
Use the current EMGS photo specification, background and dimensions. Do not reuse an old photo without checking compliance.
Offer letter
Ensure name, passport details, programme, campus and intake match the passport and application.
Academic certificates and transcripts
Prepare the documents requested for the qualification and institution; provide certified translations if required.
Health Declaration Form
Use the current form and answer all questions accurately.
Additional supporting documents
Provide any extra documents requested for the applicant’s nationality, programme or case.
Payment evidence
Keep receipts for EMGS, visa, insurance, medical screening and university charges; request a breakdown of bundled payments.

runs.t: This is a planning checklist, not a complete universal document list. The current EMGS required-documents page and the university’s international student office instructions take precedence.

sections.title: EMGS fees: understand what the total bill includes

runs.t: There is no single safe figure to quote as the complete Malaysia student visa cost for every student. The amount can depend on the application type, study duration, nationality, insurance, medical screening, Immigration charges, iKad, courier and other components. The government digital service portal currently displays an indicative range of RM2,067–RM2,638 for the student visa service. Treat this as a published service estimate, not a guaranteed invoice for every institution or case.

EMGS’s legal terms distinguish the processing fee and eVAL processing fee from medical screening, Immigration, insurance, iKad and courier charges. The terms also explain that some first-year processing and eVAL fees become non-refundable once invoiced. Ask the institution for an itemised current fee quotation and refund policy before paying.

rows.t: EMGS processing and eVAL
Which EMGS fees apply to my application and when do they become non-refundable?
Immigration / visa charges
What Student Pass, SEV or multiple-entry visa charges apply to my nationality and study period?
Medical screening
Is pre-arrival or post-arrival screening required, where must it be completed and what is the fee?
Insurance
What coverage period and policy are included? Can I choose an approved provider?
iKad and courier
Are these included in the institution’s package or billed separately?
Institution administration
Are there separate university service or handling fees?

sections.title: Cost of living in Kuala Lumpur: build a realistic monthly budget

runs.t: Kuala Lumpur can be less expensive than many major Australian study cities, but actual costs depend heavily on accommodation, commute, lifestyle and the university’s location. A student living close to campus in shared accommodation may spend much less than a student renting a private apartment and commuting across the city.

Education Malaysia’s international-student cost guide gives indicative accommodation ranges of USD50–150 per month for on-campus accommodation and USD100–300 for off-campus options. These are broad national estimates and should not be treated as a guaranteed Kuala Lumpur rent quote. Check current room listings, deposits, utilities and distance to campus before budgeting.

rows.t: Accommodation
Room in a shared apartment, residence hall or private studio.
Is rent per room or per person? Are utilities, Wi-Fi and deposits included?
Food
Mix of campus meals, local eateries, groceries and occasional restaurants.
Will you cook? Are dietary preferences likely to increase costs?
Transport
LRT/MRT/bus, student concessions where eligible, and occasional ride-hailing.
How far is the campus? Is the route walkable and reliable after evening classes?
Utilities and internet
Electricity, water, mobile plan and home broadband.
Are utilities capped or separately metered?
Study and personal
Books, printing, software, clothing, personal care and leisure.
Does the course require a laptop, specialist equipment or field trips?
One-off setup
Deposit, bedding, kitchen items, local SIM, airport transfer and initial supplies.
What is refundable and when?

runs.t: For planning, build three scenarios rather than relying on one headline “average”:

rows.t: Lean
Shared accommodation, public transport, mostly home/campus meals and limited discretionary spending.
A student prioritising affordability.
Moderate
Convenient shared accommodation, regular meals out, routine transport and some leisure.
A more balanced monthly plan.
Higher-cost
Private room or studio, more ride-hailing, frequent dining out and higher discretionary spending.
A student who values privacy and convenience.

runs.t: Do not convert a USD estimate into rupees without stating the exchange-rate date. Add a contingency for rent increases, deposits, travel and currency movement.

sections.title: Malaysia vs Australia: compare total cost and student experience

runs.t: Malaysia may offer lower living costs and a lower-cost route to selected international qualifications. Australia may offer a different labour market, campus experience, course choice and post-study pathway. A cost comparison alone cannot determine which destination is better.

rows.t: Tuition
Varies by public/private institution, course and international fee schedule; some overseas university campuses and partner pathways are available.
Varies by university, course, city and international fee schedule; confirm the exact annual fee.
Living costs
Often lower in many categories, but Kuala Lumpur rent and lifestyle vary.
Typically higher in major student cities; use current official and university estimates.
Qualification route
May include local delivery of a foreign qualification, branch campus, twinning or transfer.
Usually study at the Australian institution/campus, with course-specific delivery options.
Work rights
Student work is restricted and subject to Immigration conditions; check current rules before relying on income.
Work rights are governed by current Student visa conditions and may change.
After study
Do not assume a broad post-study work visa equivalent to another destination; verify current graduate employment and immigration routes.
Post-study options depend on current visa rules, qualification, age and other eligibility criteria.
Best comparison method
Compare the same course, duration, awarding body, accreditation and total cost.
Use the same course and assumptions to produce a fair comparison.

sections.title: Can international students work part-time in Malaysia?

runs.t: Do not build your core tuition or living-cost plan around part-time earnings. Malaysia’s student work permission is restricted and subject to conditions, including permitted locations/sectors, working-hour limits and approval processes. Rules and implementation may differ by student category and institution. Confirm the current position with Malaysian Immigration and the university’s international office before accepting any job. Working without the required permission can jeopardise Student Pass status.

sections.title: Common mistakes that delay or complicate the process

runs.t: Assuming the university offer letter itself permits entry or residence in Malaysia.
Confusing eVAL approval with the final Student Pass endorsement.
Assuming every nationality has the same SEV requirement.
Submitting a passport photo, academic record or health declaration that does not meet the current checklist.
Booking non-refundable flights before the required approval and visa steps are complete.
Assuming the advertised EMGS figure includes every insurance, medical, Immigration and institution charge.
Assuming part-time work can reliably fund tuition or living costs.

faq.q: What is the EMGS visa approval letter for Malaysia?

runs.t: The eVAL is an electronic Visa Approval Letter issued following the relevant Immigration approval process. It is a pre-arrival approval document and should not be confused with the final Student Pass endorsement.

faq.q: How long does the EMGS process take?

runs.t: Education Malaysia’s FAQ lists a 14-working-day client charter for a complete application, while the government digital service page displays 24 working days. Actual end-to-end timing varies; allow additional time for the university, corrections, any SEV and post-arrival steps.

faq.q: Can Indian students travel to Malaysia on a tourist visa and convert it to a Student Pass?

runs.t: The High Commission of India in Kuala Lumpur advises Indian students to obtain the appropriate Student Visa before arrival and says a tourist visa cannot be converted into a Student Visa after arrival. Follow the latest official entry and visa instructions.

faq.q: Is the eVAL the same as a Student Pass?

runs.t: No. The eVAL is a pre-arrival approval document. The Student Pass is the immigration permission endorsed after the required post-arrival process.

faq.q: How much money should I budget monthly in Kuala Lumpur?

runs.t: There is no single amount for every student. Build a budget using the actual accommodation quote, commute, food, utilities, course needs and personal spending. Use official estimates only as a starting point.

faq.q: Can I work while studying in Malaysia?

runs.t: Student work is restricted and subject to Immigration conditions and approval. Confirm the current rules with Immigration and your institution before working.
